extracted.intended_audience: members of the National Press Photographers Association; press/photojournalists and professional photographers
extracted.subtask_description: A professional code of ethics and disciplinary procedures for press/photojournalists, describing ethical principles (accuracy, objectivity, non-deceptive editing), duties to the public and profession, and procedures for handling violations and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership endorsement required
rubrics_metrics.description: Every member in NPPA is required to endorse the Code of Ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve the public's right to truthful information
rubrics_metrics.description: Photojournalists should respect the public's right to freedom in searching for the truth and the right to be informed truthfully and completely about public events and the world in which we live.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pictures are indispensable for keeping people accurately informed and helping the public better understand subjects in the public domain; serving the public interest is a core professional duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain the highest standards of ethical conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Photojournalists should at all times maintain the highest standards of ethical conduct in serving the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practice of photojournalism is worthy of the very best thought and effort; members should strive by example and influence to maintain high standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mercenary considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Members should maintain high ethical standards free of mercenary considerations of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photojournalists must not allow financial or promotional motives to compromise ethical standards; business promotion is acceptable but must not involve untrue statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for truthful, honest, and objective images
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the individual responsibility of every photojournalist at all times to strive for pictures that report truthfully, honestly and objectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal responsibility for accuracy and objectivity in image selection, captioning, and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter photographs in ways that deceive the public
rubrics_metrics.description: In documentary photojournalism, it is wrong to alter the content of a photograph in any way (electronically or in the darkroom) that deceives the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any alteration that changes editorial content or meaning is a breach of ethics; editing decisions should be judged by the same standards as fair and accurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fair and accurate reporting guidelines to judge electronic edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Photojournalistic guidelines for fair and accurate reporting should be the criteria for judging what may be done electronically to a photograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable electronic changes are those that do not alter editorial content or mislead viewers; preservation of historical record and accuracy is paramount.

rubrics_metrics.name: No untrue statements in business promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Business promotion in its many forms is essential but untrue statements of any nature are not worthy of a professional photojournalist and are severely condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotional activities must not include falsehoods or deceptive claims about work, awards, or credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and assist colleagues to raise quality
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the duty to encourage and assist all members of the profession, individually and collectively, so that the quality of photojournalism may constantly be raised to higher standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentorship, sharing best practices, and professional development are expected behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve freedom-of-the-press and freedom-of-access
rubrics_metrics.description: Every photojournalist must work to preserve all freedom-of-the-press rights recognized by law and to work to protect and expand freedom-of-access to all sources of news and visual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy for legal protections and practical efforts to maintain access for newsgathering are part of professional duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct business with sympathy for common humanity and societal duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of business dealings, ambitions and relations shall have in them a note of sympathy for our common humanity and shall always require consideration of our highest duties as members of society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In every business situation, the chief thought should be to fulfill responsibilities so as to lift human ideals and achievement; ethical business behavior beyond mere compliance is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply common sense and good judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: No Code of Ethics can prejudge every situation, thus common sense and good judgement are required in applying ethical principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should interpret and apply the code thoughtfully and contextually when novel or ambiguous cases arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee on Judiciary: composition and investigative role
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee on judiciary national chairman shall be appointed by the President; the Board of Directors shall appoint two additional committee members. The committee shall investigate and hear charges made against members for violations of the code or other actions detrimental to the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee is the designated body to receive, evaluate, and adjudicate complaints about ethical violations; it has authority to investigate and recommend sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint filing requirements (members accusing members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints by members, made against other members, must be signed by five active members in good standing and presented to the committee in writing, accompanied by all available facts and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complaint lacking adequate support may be rejected by majority vote; the process requires documented evidence and sufficient member endorsement to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for handling complaints against members
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a complaint the committee may reject it as inadequately supported or proceed; if proceeding, the chair will send a copy and supporting data to the accused by registered mail, notifying a reasonable time to file a sworn answer and evidence; the accused may request a personal hearing; oral testimony will be reduced to writing; if the committee majority finds charges justified the accused may be expelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The accused has rights to notice, to file a sworn answer, to present evidence, and to request a hearing; committee decisions are by majority vote and must be based on supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expulsion and right of appeal to the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: A member expelled by the committee may appeal in writing to the Board of Directors; the decision of the Board, by majority vote, shall be final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expulsion is subject to appeal but the Board's majority decision is conclusive; procedural fairness requires record submission to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for impeachment/removal of Board members
rubrics_metrics.description: Board members who willfully fail in duty or are guilty of conduct prejudicial to the association may be impeached. Complaints against a board member must be presented to the committee on judiciary in writing and endorsed by five members in good standing. The chair sends the complaint to the accused board member, failure to file an answer is considered admission; the committee may recommend removal; any board member may be suspended by majority of the committee; the Board can remove a member by two-thirds (2/3) vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impeachment follows a parallel but distinct procedure with specific voting thresholds (committee majority to recommend, board two-thirds to remove) and suspension authority; emphasis on endorsement and evidence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital manipulation principle: accuracy is the benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: As journalists we believe the guiding principle of our profession is accuracy; therefore, we believe it is wrong to alter the content of a photograph in any way that deceives the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic technologies create new challenges to integrity; preserving images as historical record is a responsibility; altering editorial content is a breach of NPPA ethical standards; fair and accurate reporting should guide permissible electronic modifications.
